Bound 4 Love

Four times, and somehow, still you.

I have experienced love before. I have experienced romance in ways I can hardly begin to explain. I have experienced it so deeply that I eventually lost the desire to participate in it altogether. I wanted to remain a mere observer of something so beautiful and genuine, someone who could appreciate it without having to become a part of it.

I could observe it. I could write about it. I could spend an unreasonable amount of time wondering what makes someone fall in love, what determines the kind of love they will experience, whether it is all left to chance, and whether we fall for the person themselves or for the things they bring into our lives—the joy, the giddiness, the anxiety, the thrill, and all the little things that make an entirely different version of ourselves possible.

I never told you this, but I have always thought of romance as something rather mundane. Crushes, infatuations, love; you name it. It is repetitive, predictable, and everywhere. I have seen it in stories, watched it unfold in other people's lives, and experienced it myself. I am not saying I have never loved anyone or anything, nor am I denying the relationships I once considered love. I simply thought I had seen enough of it to understand what it was, or at least enough to stop wondering what more there could be.

But then, you happened.

You, someone I have come to cherish so dearly. Someone who, without even trying, became special to me in ways I never quite anticipated.

For a while, I thought I needed a thousand reasons to justify the feelings that had begun to take root in me. Surely, something as significant as falling for someone must require something equally significant in return. Surely, there had to be a defining moment, a grand realization, or some extraordinary explanation for why one person could occupy so much space in another's mind.

But I was wrong.

I did not need a thousand reasons. I needed only one. One small thing. One passing gesture. One throwaway moment. One strange little detail that catches somewhere in your mind and refuses to leave. And then you think about it again. And again. Until that single thought begins to gather more thoughts around it, until something so insignificant becomes something you carry with you, until you find yourself assigning meaning to things you might never have noticed otherwise.

Perhaps that is how romanticization becomes romance. Perhaps that is how an ordinary moment becomes something worth remembering, and how someone you never intended to think about so much gradually becomes someone you cannot help but think about.

And I think, somewhere along the way, I did that with you.

Now, here I am, spilling more words than I can comfortably say aloud, trying to explain something that I cannot entirely make sense of myself. It is almost amusing, really. I have spent so much time thinking about love, studying it from a distance, turning it into words and wondering what makes it work. Yet, when it comes to understanding my own feelings, I find myself searching for an explanation that never seems quite enough.

If romance is as mundane as I once believed it to be, then how am I supposed to explain the way I feel about someone as extraordinary as you?

Perhaps I have been asking the wrong question all along. Perhaps the point was never to find some grand, irrefutable reason to justify a feeling. Perhaps I do not need to dissect every little thing until I can give it a name, nor do I need to understand every part of it before I allow myself to admit that it exists.

Because, despite all my questions, there is one thing I know.

I like you.

I like everything I have come to know about you. And I would like to know the things I have yet to discover, too, if there are still parts of yourself you would be willing to let me see. I want to learn the little details, the things you mention without thinking, the things that make you who you are. I want to know you beyond what I already know, not because I believe I can ever know everything about another person, but because knowing you has made me curious about everything else there is to know.

And I think, after all these years, perhaps I never really stopped finding my way back to you.

There is something rather unbelievable about that, isn't there? How a person can become a familiar thought, how time can pass and feelings can change, and yet somehow, you find yourself standing before the same door again, wondering whether this time you might finally have the courage to knock.

I know this may come as a surprise. Perhaps it is unexpected to hear these things from me, especially when I have spent so much time keeping them to myself. But I did not want to leave these words unwritten simply because I was afraid of what they might mean once they were out in the open. You deserve honesty, and I deserve to stop pretending that I have nothing to say.

I also wanted to tell you one last thing:

Dei, I would like to try things out with you.

That is, of course, only if you would like to let me.

I cannot tell you what your answer will make of this story. I cannot promise that I know how every page will unfold, what we might discover along the way, or what kind of ending we might eventually find ourselves writing. I only know that I would like the opportunity to write this particular part with you.

And if you say yes, I promise I will take this romance seriously. I will listen. I will observe. I will learn. I will make an effort to understand you, to communicate with you, and to give whatever we decide to begin the care and intention it deserves. I know that feelings alone cannot carry a relationship, and I do not expect them to. If we are given the chance, I want to learn how to turn these feelings into something we can both choose, nurture, and grow into together.

I am not asking you to promise me an ending. I am not asking you to give me an answer you do not mean. I simply want to know whether you might be willing to see what this could become, too.

Because I like you. Because, after all the time I have spent observing love from a distance, I find myself wanting to experience it with you, intentionally and sincerely, if you want that, too.

And perhaps that is what makes this different from everything I once believed about romance.

For all the stories I have read, all the feelings I have tried to understand, and all the words I have written about love, I have never been able to determine where a story will lead simply by looking at its first page.

But I would like to turn the page of this one with you.

If you'll let me.
